operator_scope: live camera, FIRST DESTRUCTIVE step: the writer's node was redirected at a copy for one frame. No codec ran and no format changed.

timing.note: the copy exceeds one frame budget; recording continued and both frames are intact, but this is not a rate a per-frame path can keep

notes: The first live run raised a false ERR_SOURCE: the copy used r5/r6/r7, which finish_source needs as the segment, DNG and pixel pointers. The redirect itself had already happened. Fixed by saving them around the copy.

A byte-identical mirror cannot prove itself, because a redirect that never took would put the same bytes on the card. The watermark is what makes the result decisive, and it sits in padding no decoder reads.

The copy runs at 72 MB/s, which is what an uncached write path looks like. A real writer would not copy the raster at all: it would place only the 79,872-byte header and let the codec write the payload where it already writes it.

explicitly_established.claim: the writer's node can be redirected at our own buffer: frame 1 on the card carries the watermark and frame 2 does not, so the card read our copy and not the original
CPU writes through the 0x8 uncached view are visible to the SD DMA with a dsb alone: no cache maintenance was called and the frame arrived intact
the redirected frame is a valid DNG: it decodes at 1090x1936 with the same mean as its neighbour and differs only by sensor noise
a watermark in the trailing padding after the raster does not disturb the image

explicitly_not_established: that a DIFFERENT length is accepted; seg[1] was deliberately left unchanged
anything about compressed data: no codec ran in this phase
that 44.9 ms of copying is sustainable; it is over one frame budget and only one frame was redirected
whether the uncached view would still suffice if the writer's own buffer were cached differently
more than one frame, one clip, one scene
